brief: Theodore was sixty-six years of age and a monk from Tarsus living in Italy when he was sent to England as the new Archbishop of Canterbury. The church was in disarray and dispirited, but by the time Theodore died in 690 it was well organised and confident, thanks to his wisdom and reforming zeal. He was renowned as a scholar, educationist, lover of music and administrator. He did much to resolve the differences in the English church between the older Celtic traditions and the newer Roman ones.
